Workers Earning a Living Wage or Higher

Value: Around 25 million people in Kenya still light their homes with kerosene or have no electricity at all.
We have connected 42,000 households across 14 counties, replacing kerosene lamps and reducing household energy spend by 30%.
Our systems avoided an estimated 20,000 tCO2e in 2024.
Repayment rates stay above 92% and we employ 310 staff, of whom 41% are women.
Who we serve 62% of our customers live below the national poverty line according to the Poverty Probability Index, and 71% had no electricity before buying from us.
A 2025 study by an independent evaluator compared customers with a matched control group and found 18% higher evening study hours for children and lower reported respiratory symptoms.
Over-indebtedness: we cap instalments at 10% of estimated household income and offer payment holidays after crop failures.
Over the next three years we target 150,000 connected households and 80,000 tCO2e avoided per year, and we report against IRIS+, SDG 7/1/13 and the GOGLA impact metrics.
Our carbon methodology is verified by a third-party auditor under Gold Standard rules.
